primary_claim: Framing sparse autoencoding as a latent-variable model with a variational (ELBO) objective, a full-covariance Gaussian prior (V-SAE) achieves lower reconstruction MSE (often 20-30% lower) than a standard L1-penalized SAE baseline on toy superposition benchmarks with correlated features, while maintaining comparable or higher sparsity.

effect.value: often 20-30% lower MSE for V-SAE (e.g. Case 1: 0.010 vs 0.015; Case 6: 0.025 vs 0.032)

stated_future_work: Replace the fully learned covariance with semantically structured priors (block-diagonal, graph-Laplacian) in Part II
Integrate these ideas into real-LM benchmarks
limitations_stated: Findings are from a minimal toy-model setting; validation on real language-model activations is left to later parts of the series
quote: a global-correlation prior ($\rho=0.8$) yields far cleaner feature recovery than the isotropic VAE baseline, validating our variational framework.
